title: VPC gateway conntrack slab exhaustion during private agent upgrade — follow-up and remediation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a routine private agent rolling upgrade in us-west-2, a subset of customer VPC gateways experienced a sudden spike in conntrack allocation leading to slab exhaustion on the gateway nodes. This caused transient TCP resets between control plane and agents and resulted in degraded API responsiveness for 17 customers on Dedicated/Private clusters. This ticket captures the follow-up analysis, short-term mitigations we applied, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-01-25 02:14 UTC: Scheduled rolling upgrade started for private-agents v2.27 in us-west-2 cluster group A
2025-01-25 02:43 UTC: First gateway node reported high conntrack count and started dropping new connections
2025-01-25 02:50 UTC: Control plane observed elevated API error rates and increased latency; automated alert fired
2025-01-25 03:05 UTC: Rollout paused. On-call network engineer performed initial triage and confirmed conntrack exhaustion on 6/12 gateway nodes
2025-01-25 03:25 UTC: Emergency mitigation: reduced per-node agent concurrency and rebalanced traffic away from affected gateways via routing weights
2025-01-25 04:10 UTC: Stabilization observed; API error rates returned to baseline for most customers. Incident declared mitigated at 04:30 UTC
2025-01-25 08:00 UTC: Root cause investigation started; heap of kernel conntrack allocations correlated with a new session keep-alive behavior in agent v2.27
root_cause: A code change in private agent v2.27 introduced aggressive per-session persistent connections with delayed FIN handling during background health-checks. Combined with an upstream kernel change in the gateway AMI that reduced default conntrack table size on node restart, connection entries accumulated faster than the garbage-collection threshold, exhausting the conntrack slab and causing new TCP handshakes to fail.
mitigations_taken: Paused rolling upgrade and reverted agent rollout to v2.26 for remaining nodes in the batch
Temporarily reduced agent keepalive interval and lowered per-agent concurrency (config override) for affected clusters
Applied emergency sysctl bump for net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on impacted gateway nodes to prevent immediate re-exhaustion
Rerouted traffic by adjusting routing weights so that healthy gateways absorbed burst while affected nodes drained
Created alert for conntrack usage crossing 60% of capacity with automated routing-weight rollback to throttle new sessions
action_items: ENG-NET-1: Stabilize default AMI kernel config — ensure nf_conntrack_max is set to baseline that matches instance type recommendations (owner: Lina Chen, estimate: 3, due: 2025-02-05)
ENG-RUNTIME-2: Revert or patch agent v2.27 keepalive behavior; land PR that sets FIN timeout to previous behavior under private-deploy flag (owner: Miguel Soto, estimate: 5, due: 2025-02-12)
ENG-OBS-3: Add conntrack saturation SLO + dashboard tile per-cluster and per-gateway node (owner: Noah Brooks, estimate: 3, due: 2025-02-14)
ENG-AUTO-4: Implement preflight check in private rollout pipeline to validate conntrack headroom based on instance type and current load (owner: Asha Patel, estimate: 5, due: 2025-02-18)

ENG-RUNBOOK-5: Update Private Deploy runbook with step-by-step mitigation for conntrack exhaustion including sysctl bump, traffic reroute, and rollback guidance (owner: Lina Chen, estimate: 2, due: 2025-02-07)
ENG-SIGCOMM-6: Add automated canary that exercises long-lived sessions during agent upgrades to detect pathological keepalive patterns (owner: Miguel Soto, estimate: 8, due: 2025-03-03)
ENG-SEC-7: Audit security implications of sysctl adjustments and document required approvals for customers on FIPS/HIPAA environments (owner: Priya Nambiar, estimate: 2, due: 2025-02-20)
acceptance_criteria: Conntrack headroom preflight added to rollout pipeline and verified on 3 instance families
Agent v2.27 keepalive patch merged and rolled to a small canary with no conntrack increase after 24h
Dashboard and alerting for conntrack usage visible in Console with 1-hour and 5-minute aggregations
Runbook updated and reviewed by on-call network and private-deploy owners
risks: Raising nf_conntrack_max without addressing root cause may only postpone exhaustion under heavy sustained load
Automated sysctl changes could conflict with customer-managed node hardening policies in some private/on-prem setups
Aggressive canary tests might generate noisy traffic affecting customer SLAs if not properly scoped
